summary: VERIFIED: the repo exists and is an original, Apache-2.0 Rust rewrite of RA2 by one author (GitHub user oovm, a.k.a. Aster / SasakiSaki). It has 1,662 commits and about 103K lines of Rust (about 30K of them tests). It is a desktop native app (winit + wgpu, loaded as an N-API addon from a Node CLI), not a working web game: the ra-wasm browser binding does not even depend on ra-engine, ra-map or ra-widgets. Gameplay is an early vertical slice. Implemented: a skirmish loop with MCV deploy, construction, production queues, harvesting and economy, power, tech tree, repair, capture, infiltrate, a basic heuristic AI plus minimal AITrigger/TeamType execution, and 11 map trigger event types. Missing in code: projectiles and splash damage (combat is instant damage at cell-Manhattan range), fog/shroud, garrisons, runtime veterancy, every superweapon except Lightning Storm, naval and bridge gameplay, multiplayer, save/load, replays, and explosion effects. Campaign boot deliberately refuses maps with unsupported trigger events or actions. The 'renderer' is really a CPU compositor: ra-map paints terrain, overlays, buildings and even moving units into one full-map RGBA bitmap, and wgpu uploads it as one texture drawn with a single textured-quad WGSL shader. For HD work the GPU renderer would have to be built almost from scratch. On the plus side the engine/render split via RenderSnapshot is clean, and the Westwood format decoders (MIX crypto, SHP, TMP, VXL/HVA/VPL, CSF, AUD/BAG, and a native Rust Bink decoder) are reusable. The git history's dates are fabricated: an even ~1 commit/day from 2013-01-23 to 2017-08-12, including an impossible 2014 dependabot commit, but the repo was actually created 2026-09-06. Build: the native addon compiles in 85 s on stable Rust 1.96 and 728 asset-free tests pass. The full `pnpm run build` fails (wasm-pack is not installed and the TS host needs the wasm package), and the release .node fails to load on macOS 27.2 until symbol stripping is turned off.
license_evidence: VERIFIED: (1) /License.md is the full 'Apache License ... Version 2.0, January 2004' text. (2) The root package.json has "license": "Apache-2.0". (3) Cargo.toml [workspace.package] has license = "Apache-2.0" and authors = ["Aster <192607617@qq.com>"], and every crate inherits license.workspace. (4) The host package projects/hosts/red-alert2/package.json has "license": "Apache-2.0" (but also "private": true, version 0.0.0). (5) The README section '许可与数据' says '引擎源代码： **Apache-2.0**'. (6) The GitHub API reports license spdx_id Apache-2.0. Missing: there is no NOTICE file and no per-file copyright headers. Game assets are not included (README: '仓库 **不包含**原版 MIX / INI / 音频 / 地图等资源文件'). A minor note: ra-assets/data/mix_known_names.txt (83,352 file names, embedded via include_str! in src/mix/names.rs) is described as 'engine-referenced names + public INI references'. It has no attribution and may overlap with community name databases such as XCC's. That is low risk, since these are lists of retail file names.
provenance: Original work by a single author (GitHub user oovm, also 'SasakiSaki' / 'Aster'). It shows no signs of being derived from Chrono Divide or of being a decompilation. The commit history was rewritten with fabricated timestamps. INFERENCE: the code was very likely written largely with AI coding agents, in small agent-sized increments.
provenance_evidence: VERIFIED: (a) The first commit 335645b3 is a small skeleton (35 files, 1,326 insertions: ra-types, ra-assets stub mix.rs/ini.rs, ra-desktop main.rs, ra-renderer 29 lines). Features then arrive incrementally over 1,661 more commits ('Parse encrypted MIX archives', 'Add SHP(TS) sprite parser', 'Add TMP isometric tile parser', 'Decode IsoMapPack5' ...). That is the opposite of a single giant import of a finished engine. (b) The language is Rust. Chrono Divide is closed-source TypeScript. There are no mentions of chronodivide/openra/ra2web anywhere, and no gamemd.exe hex addresses (0 matches for 0x004xxxxx–0x007xxxxx), so nothing points to decompilation. Custom identifiers (LEPTONS_PER_CELL, rasterize_vxl, VxlLayerPose, house_remap, PresentFeel) appear 0 times in the TS candidate repos DD-Channel/ra2-web, OpenRA2/RA2Web, huangkaoya/ts-redalert2, ra2-games/ra2 and TaiYouWeb/ra2. The only shared strings are retail format section names (IsoMapPack5, OverlayDataPack). The simulation's design (cell-Manhattan range, instant damage, BFS pathing, 15 Hz ticks) is idiosyncratic and much simpler than CD's. (c) Author background: GitHub user oovm (name SasakiSaki, company Tencent, Shanghai, 692 followers, 315 repos, account created 2016). The same org and author have earlier RA2 tooling: ra2-remixer, vxl-renderer (D3D12), rs-ddraw, relert.js-browser, YurisHook, FontsForRedAlert2, ra2-tools, dated 2024–2025. So there is real domain history. (d) Fabricated dates: `git log` author and committer dates run from 2013-01-23 to 2017-08-12. They are spread almost perfectly evenly, averaging 86,411 s (one day) between commits, 22–38 per month. That is impossible given the code uses Rust edition 2024 and wgpu 30.0.1. The dependabot[bot] commit 086f0696 is dated 2014-04-09. The .gitignore contains 'time-travel.*'. The GitHub API says created_at 2026-09-06T18:18:02Z and pushed_at 2026-09-15, and the repo was generated from the template oovm/RustTemplate (created 2017-04-20). Commit author emails are galaster@foxmail.com (170) and aster@vers.site (1,491), all mapped by GitHub to oovm. INFERENCE: the dates were deliberately rewritten, and the motive is unknown. This does not affect licensing, but it is a trust and transparency red flag. (e) AI-agent style: gitmoji micro-commits, and README instructions aimed at an agent ('资源查证：用 extract / unpack，不要再写一次性 Rust 探针', '原生壳：只走 TypeScript CLI（不要 cargo run / Rust bin / example）'). The crate READMEs are also unusually uniform.
tech_stack: VERIFIED: Rust workspace (resolver 2, edition 2024). rust-toolchain.toml pins nightly, but no #![feature] is used and it builds on stable 1.96. About 820 .rs files and 103K lines across 16 crates plus 4 adaptors: ra-types, ra-ecs, ra-assets, ra-config, ra-map, ra-engine, ra-net, ra-renderer, ra-layout, ra-widgets, ra-adaptor{,-ra2,-yuri,-phobos}, ra-napi, ra-wasm, ra-testing. Key dependencies: wgpu 30.0.1 (features=webgl), winit 0.30, pollster, napi 3 / napi-derive 3 (napi4), wasm-bindgen 0.2 / web-sys, rodio 0.22 (playback only), symphonia 0.6.1 (wav/pcm), image 0.25, blowfish 0.10 + num-bigint 0.5 (MIX index crypto), serde/serde_json, encoding_rs, tracing. JS side: pnpm 9.15.4 workspace, TypeScript ^5.8 (5.9.3 resolved), biome 2.5.12, and a Node CLI host at projects/hosts/red-alert2/bin/ra2.mjs. No Cargo.lock is committed (it is gitignored), so Rust dependency versions are not pinned. There is no three.js or any web framework.
renderer_architecture:
VERIFIED in code. Asset decode (ra-assets):
- mix/ has a CRC Westwood name hash, RSA+Blowfish index decryption ('同族 ccmix') and MixVfs layered/nested mounts.
- image/ has PAL, SHP(TS) with RLE-zero, TMP isometric tiles, PCX, FNT, CSF, and a full native Bink video decoder (bink_*.rs, about 2.3K lines).
- voxel/ has VXL, HVA and VPL parsers. voxel/raster.rs does 'VXL 简易等距正交投影（预览用；车身 VPL 为法线→亮度页粗映射）': a CPU orthographic rasterization with 8-way yaw, multiple layers (body/turret/barrel) and a projected shadow.
- audio/ has AUD IMA-ADPCM, BAG and WAV.
- rules/ has techno, warheads, super_weapons, countries, color_schemes and house_remap.

House colours: rules/house_remap.rs remaps palette indices 16..31 from rules [Colors] HSV, applied through remap_owner_palette in ra-napi host/boot.rs.

World drawing is CPU compositing in ra-map: compose.rs/terrain_paint.rs (TMP terrain plus terrain anims), overlay_paint.rs (ore, walls, bridges drawn in a separate bridge layer), structure_paint.rs (SHP/VXL buildings, damage frames, anims) and mobile_paint.rs (units: VXL via rasterize_vxl_layer_poses, or SHP). Map [Lighting] (ambient, RGB, Ground/Level, Ion profile, point lights, per-cell tint) is baked on the CPU (lighting.rs, radiation_light.rs). Weather is CPU particles painted into the bitmap (weather_particles.rs): snow only by default in the snow theater, with Fog and Rain types available.

The output is one full-map RgbaImage. ra-renderer (only about 2.9K lines) uploads it as a single texture (sprite.rs, one WGSL shader: textured quad, nearest sampling, alpha blend, sRGB). On top it draws health pips and brackets from pips.shp/pipbrd.shp (markers.rs), order icons (order_icons.rs), and one CPU-composited HUD page texture. There are 1–2 render passes, no depth buffer, and no per-object GPU draw calls.

Moving units are baked into the base map. battle_controller/render.rs calls rebuild_preview_base_with_mobiles and re-uploads the full texture whenever mobiles move or slide ('移动单位烤在预览底图上'). pass.rs PassGraph (Terrain/Overlay/Objects/Effects/Ui/Minimap) is self-described as '骨架…尚未接通真实 pass 录制'. No projectile, explosion or effect rendering exists. The camera (camera.rs) is a 2D pan/zoom over the composited image, not an isometric projection matrix.

GPU backend: wgpu Backends::PRIMARY (Metal on macOS; DX12/Vulkan elsewhere), Fifo present. The browser WebGL2 path is only attachCanvas/presentFrame in ra-wasm.

Netcode: ra-net is 387 lines of protocol-agnostic types and length-prefixed framing, with no sockets and no lockstep scheduler. ra-engine has a deterministic FNV-style state digest (persistence/digest.rs) and fixed 15 Hz ticks (DEFAULT_TICK_HZ = 15).

Audio: rodio device playback with music and SFX volume, plus EVA advice. Video: a Bink menu-movie player (ra-widgets chrome/movie.rs); the PlayMovie and PlayIngameMovie trigger actions are no-op stubs.

UI: retail-style shell screens (splash, main, single, campaign, skirmish lobby, choose map, options, battle HUD sidebar with cameos, pause menu, score screen), composed on the CPU with retail SHP, FNT and CSF.
activity: VERIFIED via GitHub API (2026-09-27): 294 stars, 15 forks, 2 subscribers. Contributors: oovm with 1,661 commits and dependabot[bot] with 1. Real dates: created 2026-09-06, last push 2026-09-15; star and fork events continued daily up to 2026-09-27. Git-recorded dates are fabricated (2013-01-23 first, 2017-08-12 last). Issues are disabled (has_issues=false, open_issues=0); Discussions are enabled. There are no releases or tags. npm @game-gpt/red-alert2 returns E404 (rechecked with `npm view` on 2026-09-27), and the host package.json is "private": true at version 0.0.0. CI workflows exist (ci.yml with a 3-OS native build and tests plus a Linux wasm job, and publish-npm.yml), but I did not verify CI run status. The org rust-alert also created terraria.exe (2026-09-19) and hl.exe (2026-09-23), both with 0 stars, which suggests the author's attention is spreading across 'X.exe' rewrites.
build_result:
Run on an M5 Pro, macOS 27.2, Node 26.0.0, Homebrew cargo/rustc 1.96.0 stable, no rustup; CARGO_HOME and the pnpm store were placed in the scratchpad.
(1) `pnpm install`: OK in 25 s (3 dev dependencies: biome 2.5.12, typescript 5.9.3, and the workspace host).
(2) `pnpm run build` (the production build = build:wasm → build:ts → build:napi): FAILED immediately at build:wasm with spawn wasm-pack ENOENT, because wasm-pack is not installed. Homebrew rustc also has only the aarch64-apple-darwin target, with no wasm32-unknown-unknown and no rustup to add it.
(3) `pnpm run build:napi` (cargo build --release -p ra-napi): SUCCEEDED in 85 s with 7 warnings in ra-napi (dead code such as toggle_window_fullscreen) and 1 in ra-map. It produced an 8.5 MB red-alert2.darwin-arm64.node. However, `require()` of that file FAILED with dlopen 'mis-aligned LINKEDIT string pool, fileOffset=0x00808DA4', caused by the release profile's strip = "symbols" on this macOS/dyld.
(4) Rebuilding with CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_STRIP=none took 62 s and the addon then loads. It exports [unpack, emulate, extract, version, diagnoseMaps], and version() returns '0.1.0'.
(5) `pnpm run build:ts`: FAILED with TS2307 "Cannot find module '@game-gpt/red-alert2-unknown-wasm32'" in src/wasm.ts lines 3 and 21, because the wasm package was never built.
(6) `pnpm exec ra2 --help` works and lists the emulate/extract/unpack/diagnose-maps commands.
(7) `cargo test -p ra-assets -p ra-map -p ra-engine -p ra-testing`: 728 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored (188 assets, 1+303 engine, 214 map, 22 testing), in 12 s including compile.
I could not run `ra2 emulate` because no RA2 game files are on this machine, so actual playability and visuals are UNVERIFIED. Logs are in scratchpad/repos/rustalert_{install,build,napi,napi_nostrip,ts,test}.log.
feature_completeness:
V = verified in code, R = README claim only, X = verified absent.
- Web/browser version: X. ra-wasm (696 lines) has only canvas attach/present, audio resume and install-file ingestion. Its Cargo.toml does not depend on ra-engine, ra-map or ra-widgets. projects/sites/playground only depends on the unpublished npm package.
- Allied/Soviet campaign: partial and likely blocked. V: a campaign screen and open_campaign_session_prepared exist, and battle.ini/mission.ini are parsed. But only 11 trigger EVENT types are recognized (codes 1, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 30, 48, 52), and campaign boot is refused whenever an unsupported event or action appears (ra-map scripting/capability.rs campaign_blocking_capability_message; ra-napi host/boot.rs around line 645). About 24 actions (PlayMovie, RevealAllMap, GrowShroud, PlaySpeech, TextTrigger, CenterCamera...) are no-op stubs (engine gameplay/triggers.rs around line 611). INFERENCE: most retail missions will not start.
- YR content: V for edition detection and resource chains (ra-adaptor-yuri: ra2md.mix, rulesmd.ini, expandmd*). X for YR mechanics: mind control has 1 incidental match and no system.
- Skirmish vs AI: V, and it is the main path: lobby, MCV deploy, construction and placement, production queues per category, harvesters and economy, power (low power halves production), tech tree, repair, sell cursor, capture, infiltrate, starting units, win/lose. AI quality is weak: heuristic build plus army cap HEURISTIC_ARMY_CAP=8, producing every 45 ticks, plus minimal [AITriggerTypes]/TeamTypes/ScriptTypes execution (gameplay/ai.rs, ai_triggers.rs, script_teams.rs).
- Online/LAN multiplayer: X (ra-net has types and framing only).
- All units/buildings/superweapons: partial. Definitions are rules-driven, but combat is instant hit at cell-Manhattan range with Verses vs armor (gameplay/combat.rs). X for projectile simulation and CellSpread splash (0 matches). Superweapons: only LIGHTNINGSTORM fires; every other type returns FireSuperWeaponError::UnsupportedKind (gameplay/powers.rs around line 369).
- Naval units and water: X. Naval units are skipped by the AI and starting units, and there is no water rendering or naval locomotion.
- Bridges: visual only (overlay_paint.rs bridge layer), with no bridge simulation or destruction.
- Garrisoning: X (0 matches for garrison or Occupier).
- Veterancy: X at runtime (parsed only from map TeamTypes VeteranLevel).
- Chronosphere, Iron Curtain and other special abilities: X.
- Fog and shroud: X in the engine (only trigger enum stubs).
- Custom maps: V for loading retail and install maps, and the diagnose-maps CLI. .yrm is not specifically verified.
- Sound, EVA and music: V (AUD/BAG/WAV decode, rodio playback, EVA advice, music and SFX volume).
- FMV: V for a native Bink decoder and the menu movie. X for mission and in-game movies (stubs).
- Save/load: X (persistence/save.rs and restore.rs are 1-line files).
- Replays: X.
- INI modding: V (rules/art/ai INI parse and merge, then RuntimeDefinitions). Phobos/MO support is layout detection only; extended INI semantics are unimplemented.
- Map editor: X.
- Performance at high resolution: V for windowed/fullscreen and zoom. INFERENCE: it will likely scale poorly, because the whole map bitmap is recomposited on the CPU and re-uploaded whenever units move.
- Pathfinding: V, but it is a plain BFS on one pass grid (ra-map pass_grid.rs find_path) with no locomotor layers.
asset_requirements:
The user must own a retail RA2 (and optionally YR) install. They point the CLI at it with `ra2 emulate --path <dir> --edition ra2|yr`, or set ra2_dir in ~/Library/Application Support/rust-alert2/settings.json (overridable with RUST_ALERT2_DATA_DIR). VERIFIED file lists from the adaptors:
- RA2 root: language.mix, ra2.mix, multi.mix, theme.mix, maps01.mix, maps02.mix.
- Nested inside those: local.mix, cache.mix, conquer.mix, generic.mix, isogen.mix, cameo.mix, audio.mix, neutral.mix, load.mix, sidec01/02.mix, sidenc01/02.mix, plus theater mixes (e.g. isotemp.mix).
- INI and text: rules.ini, art.ini, ui.ini, sound.ini, eva.ini, mpmodes.ini, battle.ini, mission.ini, ai.ini, ra2.csf.
- YR adds: langmd.mix, ra2md.mix, multimd.mix, thememd.mix, mapsmd01–03.mix, the expandmd*.mix layers, and the rulesmd/artmd/aimd INI files. Mixed installs need --edition set explicitly.
- Mental Omega: detected via Phobos.dll or MO client files only.
Browser: the design has JavaScript feed files by name into an InstallSession (ra-wasm host/install.rs), but this is not wired to gameplay. No assets are needed to build. The project ships no game assets.
hd_extensibility:
Good seams, but the renderer would need to be rebuilt almost from scratch. Specific points:

1) Clean contract. ra-engine exports RenderSnapshot/SnapshotUnit (engine src/game/snapshot.rs) plus dirty sets (presentation/dirty.rs), and ra-renderer only consumes those. A new GPU world renderer can be written against that contract without touching the simulation. EASY to reuse, but the contract lacks projectile, explosion and effect data, because the engine has none.

2) Hi-res sprite replacement: today every drawable is painted on the CPU into one bitmap (ra-map terrain_paint.rs, overlay_paint.rs, structure_paint.rs, mobile_paint.rs; ra-napi battle_controller/render.rs rebuild_preview_base_with_mobiles). You would replace these with GPU instanced sprite batches in new ra-renderer modules: terrain.rs, objects.rs and effects.rs, which the renderer README lists as 'future' entries. Then add a texture-atlas loader that picks an HD PNG/KTX2 override keyed by SHP, TMP or VXL name and frame before falling back to palette decode (ra-assets image/shp, image/tmp). HARD: 4–8 weeks of engineering, because depth-sorting of isometric objects, cell heights and bridges must be re-implemented on the GPU. ra-map iso.rs, playfield.rs and the cell_z helpers in compose.rs give the math.

3) VXL to real-time mesh: ra-assets voxel/vxl.rs, hva.rs and vpl.rs already parse sections, normals and HVA matrices. Replace voxel/raster.rs (CPU ortho splat) with GPU greedy-meshing or instanced voxels, per-section HVA transforms, and normal-based lighting with an orthographic isometric camera. MEDIUM–HARD: 2–4 weeks. The author's separate repo rust-alert/vxl-renderer (D3D12) may hold prior art; I did not inspect it.

4) Normal/depth-map lighting: map [Lighting] parsing and per-cell tint already exist (ra-map lighting.rs LightingConfig, PointLight, Ion profile). Pass them as uniforms or a light texture to a deferred or forward+ pass over G-buffer sprites (albedo + normal + height). This needs normal and height maps authored or AI-generated for every sprite. HARD, and gated by asset volume.

5) Post-processing: pass.rs PassGraph is only an enum skeleton, and the frame currently has 1–2 passes with no depth or HDR. You would add an offscreen HDR target plus bloom, tone-mapping, color grading and TAA/FXAA in ra-renderer lib.rs submit_frame. MEDIUM: 1–2 weeks once the world is drawn on the GPU.

6) Water shader: nothing exists (no water tile classification or animation). Tag water TMP tiles from the theater INI and tileset (ra-map tileset.rs, theater.rs) and draw them with a dedicated animated normal-mapped or screen-space-reflection water pass. MEDIUM, 2–3 weeks.

7) Weather: ra-map weather_particles.rs is CPU dots and streaks. Port it to GPU compute particles, add screen-space rain, fog volumes and wet-surface shading, and tie it to Ion storm / LightingProfile. MEDIUM.

8) GPU particles and impact effects: this is blocked on the simulation. The engine has no projectile entities, warhead AnimList or explosion events, so combat.rs has to emit weapon, projectile and impact events first, and then a GPU particle system in ra-renderer can consume them. HARD, because it is simulation plus rendering work.

9) Advantages: wgpu 30 runs natively on Metal on the M5 and could target WebGPU/WebGL2 for the browser, all in one Rust codebase. Disadvantages: the browser build is not wired (roughly 2–4 weeks to connect engine, map, widgets and input through ra-wasm, plus handling multi-hundred-MB MIX uploads and wasm memory). The HUD and UI are also CPU-composited bitmaps (ra-widgets), so HD UI means redoing that path too.
risks: Not a web game: the browser path (ra-wasm) has no engine, map or UI wiring. It fails the user's 'build on the existing web version' premise, and wiring it up means 2–4+ weeks of work plus solving large MIX ingestion and wasm memory in the browser.

Gameplay far from original: no projectiles or splash, fog/shroud, garrison, veterancy, Chronosphere, Iron Curtain, Nuke or other superweapons (only Lightning Storm), naval, bridge gameplay, multiplayer, save/load or replays. Campaign maps are refused at boot when they use any of the ~50 unrecognized trigger events. Faithful 'Step 1' parity would take many months.

The renderer is a CPU compositor: moving units are baked into a full-map bitmap that is re-uploaded to the GPU. The HD work (hi-res sprites, VXL meshes, lighting, water, particles, post-FX) needs a new GPU renderer, so very little of the renderer is reusable.

Trust and transparency: git timestamps are fabricated (evenly one per day, 2013–2017, including an impossible 2014 dependabot commit), while the repo is actually 3 weeks old (created 2026-09-06). There is a single author with a pattern of spawning many 'X.exe' rewrite repos, which makes long-term maintenance uncertain.

Likely heavily AI-agent-generated code: it is internally consistent and well tested (728 tests), but semantics may drift from real RA2 behaviour and the architecture is still in flux ('过渡期', many skeleton modules).
Bus factor of 1, issues disabled, no releases, no published npm package (the host is private: true), and no Cargo.lock committed, so builds are not reproducible.

Build friction on this Mac: the release profile's strip="symbols" produces a .node that macOS 27.2 dyld rejects (mis-aligned LINKEDIT), needing CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_STRIP=none. The full build also needs rustup + nightly + wasm32 target + wasm-pack, none of which are installed.
Unattributed 83K-entry MIX filename list (ra-assets/data/mix_known_names.txt), which may derive from community databases. Minor licensing hygiene issue.
Nothing could be verified visually or for playability, because no RA2 assets are on the machine. All playability conclusions come from code reading.
score_rationale:
Legality (strong, +): Apache-2.0 throughout, original Rust code with no Chrono Divide or decompilation signals, and assets are bring-your-own. This is the cleanest licensing I have seen among RA2 web candidates.

Completeness of original gameplay (weak, −−): only a skirmish vertical slice works. Core RA2 systems are missing (projectiles, fog, garrisons, veterancy, superweapons, naval, multiplayer, save/load), and campaigns are gated off by unsupported triggers.

Web requirement (fails, −−): the browser build is a placeholder.

Renderer upgradability (mixed, −): the RenderSnapshot contract and the wgpu 30 choice (Metal now, WebGPU later) suit an HD path well. But the actual renderer is a CPU bitmap blitter of about 2.9K lines, so HD means writing the GPU renderer from scratch.

Code quality (moderate, +): modular crates, extensive Chinese documentation, 728 passing tests, and the native build works on stable Rust. On the other hand the architecture is still in flux and appears agent-generated.

Activity and trust (weak, −): about 9 days of real pushes, one author, fabricated commit dates, issues disabled, no releases.

Net: the format decoders (MIX, SHP, TMP, VXL, HVA, CSF, AUD, Bink) and parts of the simulation skeleton could be mined as a legally clean library. As the base for 'get the original game running on the web, then remaster it in HD' it would need most of the gameplay, the web binding and the entire GPU renderer built out. That makes it barely better than starting from scratch in Rust, hence 3/10.
